The Exchange had sought clarification from NMDC Limited with respect to a news item captioned "NMDC to lay Rs 800 cr slurry pipeline for Nagarnar plant". The Company has clarified as follows :  NMDC has initiated activities to develop 15 MTPA Slurry Pipeline System from Bailadila to Vizag for transportation of iron ore fines in slurry form after its conversion to iron ore concentrate suitable for making Pellets. Around 2 MTPA iron ore concentrate will be offloaded in NMDC s Steel Plant premises at Nagarnar for converting the iron ore concentrate into Pellets in the proposed Pellet Plant at Nagarnar. The balance iron ore concentrate will be transported to Vizag.     The project shall be executed in two parts as below:  (i) In the State of Chhattisgarh, Slurry Pipeline System from Bailadila to Nagarnar along with Ore processing plants at Bailadila and Pellet Plant at Nagarnar will be owned and set up by NMDC. The configuration of the Project is as below:  (1) 6 MTPA Ore Processing Plant at Kirandul & 4 MTPA Ore Processing Plant at Bacheli;  (2) 11 MTPA Capacity Slurry Pipeline System from Kirandul to Bacheli;  (3) 15 MTPA capacity Slurry Pipeline System from Bacheli to Nagarnar;  (4) 2 MTPA Pellet Plant along with filtration plant at Nagarnar;   (5) Associated Feed water and Electrical Power supply systems for the Project;   (6) Return Water Pipeline system from Nagarnar to Bacheli     The capex for the above portion of the Project is approximately Rs 4000 crores    (ii) Slurry Pipeline System from Nagarnar to Vizag along with Pellet Plant at Vizag shall be set up under JV in which NMDC and RINL will be prime partners. Selection of other partners for participation in the project is in progress. After selection of other partners, JV Company will be formed. The configuration of the Project shall be as below:   (1) 13 MTPA Capacity Slurry Pipeline System from Nagarnar to Vizag;  (2) 6 MTPA Pellet Plant at Vizag;  (3) 8 MTPA filtration Plant at Vizag;  (4) Return Water Pipeline system from Vizag to Nagarnar   The capex for the above portion of the Project is approximately Rs 6000 crores.
